title: Introduce traffic-splitting plugin and automated rollback hooks for staged model rollouts
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds a traffic-splitting plugin and server-side automated rollback hooks for staged rollouts; exposes canary health gating metrics to the Console; backwards compatible with existing rollout policies
description:
Motivation: We need a lightweight, centralized way to run staged model rollouts (canary/A-B/shadow) that supports: weighted traffic-splitting, programmable health gates (latency, error-rate, regressed quality), synthetic traffic injection for validation, and deterministic automated rollback hooks. This PR implements a server-side traffic-splitting plugin and a generic rollback hook framework so rollout policies can declare health gates that trigger an automated rollback and post-mortem ticket creation.

What this changes (high level):
- New runtime plugin: pkg/rollout/plugin/traffic_split.go (weighted routing at request-proxy layer, supports fractional weights, priority fallbacks)
- Health gating infra: pkg/rollout/health/gates.go (pluggable gate types: latency_p95, error_rate, eval-regression)
- Rollback hooks: pkg/rollout/hooks/rollback.go + integrations with notifications and Linear (minimal adapter)
- Synthetic traffic generator: tools/trafficgen/canary_driver.go (replay and synthetic workload profiles for SLA validation)
- Console: console/src/routes/rollouts/preview.tsx to show split ratios and real-time gate metrics
- Tests and CI: integration tests for canary path, unit tests for plugin and hooks, e2e smoke for Console view

Checklist: 
- [x] Traffic-splitting plugin implementation + unit tests
- [x] Health gate API and a latency/error_rate gate impl
- [x] Rollback hook framework + Linear adapter (no credentials shipped)
- [x] Synthetic traffic generator and CI integration test
- [x] Console display for rollouts and gate metrics
- [x] Docs: docs/runbooks/rollouts.md with new failure scenarios and runbook steps

Backward compatibility: The traffic-splitting plugin registers as an optional runtime plugin. Existing rollout policies that do not opt-in retain current behavior. No wire-level API changes to the public Redwood API; rollout configuration is an internal service-level extension.

Performance notes: The routing path is optimized for the common fast-path: when weight=100% it compiles to a direct forward (no additional allocations). Fractional traffic uses a consistent-hash + token-bucket approach to maintain session stickiness without per-request storage. Benchmarks in benchmark-lab show median additional latency <0.6ms on our internal perf-canary for 128-byte payloads.

Testing summary (CI):
- unit-tests: pass
- lint: pass
- integration/canary: initially failed due to a race in synthetic driver; fixed by introducing deterministic seeding and re-run -> pass
- e2e/console: pass on first run

Rollout and merge plan: After review and sign-off we merged via squash. The feature is gated behind a feature flag (rollout.traffic_split.enabled) and a default policy that is off for existing customers. We will enable only for internal canaries in the next week and progressively for beta tenants.

Related work: ENG-4921 (unified rollout requirements), PM-128 (product acceptance criteria), previous experiments in perf-canary for staged traffic (see pr refs in runbook).

Notes for reviewers: Pay attention to the gates.go API boundary — it's intentionally minimal to avoid coupling eval infra. The rollback hook intentionally emits a compact JSON payload to the Linear adapter; teams wanting richer context should extend the adapter (small example in docs/runbooks/rollouts.md).

Merge outcome: merged to main via squash on 2026-02-15 after approvals from Ethan and Sofia and a green CI run.
commits: feat(rollout): add traffic-splitting plugin and registration
feat(rollout): add health gate primitives and latency_p95 gate
feat(rollout): rollback hook framework + linear adapter (no creds)
test(rollout): integration test for staged canary path with synthetic driver
docs(runbooks): document rollout failure scenarios and mitigation steps
console: add rollout preview pane and gate metrics UI
review_conversation:
Ethan Rivera: Can the traffic-split logic guarantee per-session stickiness across autoscaling events?
Priya Nair: Yes — we use consistent-hash by session id and include node affinity token; when nodes are rescheduled we fall back to weighted reassign which is rare and documented. Added comments and a test for deterministic reassign.
Sofia Martinez: Are gate thresholds configurable per-tenant?
Priya Nair: Yes, gates are per-rollout config and we expose them in the console; the default system policy used by internal canaries is conservative.
Benji Kline: The Linear adapter includes only a summary — will we ever need full request traces?
Priya Nair: We decided to keep the adapter small to avoid leaking PII in tickets. There is an opt-in trace dump hook for support-driven escalations (disabled by default).
Sofia Martinez: Approved after addressing CI flake and adding docs.
Ethan Rivera: Approved after minor comments and bench numbers added to the PR description.
